clue.text: Drunk amused when leader is changed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for amused is swapped for a different one

parts.note: amused means tickled

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy finds things funny until a new boss takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leader is changed' swaps the T at the front of TICKLED for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is a slang synonym for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Bird finally landing, breathing heavily

parts.note: a puffin is a seabird

indicators.note: takes the last letter of landing

explanation.surface: A bird puffs hard as it finally comes down to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffing means panting, taking short heavy breaths.

clue.text: Weep quietly — it's over Charlie's description of this crossword?

parts.note: to cry is to weep
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: over says the word it is reversed

parts.note: the word it, with is as the link
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A solver weeps softly; it is all over Charlie's description of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic crossword is one with puzzling, riddling clues, as this one is.

clue.text: Discover manager's back in bank

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does

indicators.note: takes the last letter of manager

explanation.surface: Finding the manager has returned to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; it is the verb meaning tilt. 'back' gives R, put 'in' LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to discover or find it out.

clue.text: Troublesome pants could fit if nothing's removed

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for nothing is taken out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Awkward trousers might fit once nothing more is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for poor) rearranges COULD FIT IF once 'removed' takes out O.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult and troublesome both describe something hard to deal with.

clue.text: Ship commander's hat — one with brown on the outside

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

indicators.note: the brown word sits around the one, enclosing it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Describing a sea captain's headgear: a cap with brown trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one with brown on the outside' means the brown word wraps around the numeral, not that brown follows one.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the officer in command of a vessel.

clue.text: Held top of church organ

indicators.note: takes the first letter of church, the top in a down clue

parts.note: a lung is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: The best church organ was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, to have held on tightly.

clue.text: Cooler tenants?

parts.note: cooler is slang for a prison, so its occupants are inmates

explanation.surface: Residents who are more chilled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates of a jail live there involuntarily, as residents of the clink.

clue.text: Measures adult horses

parts.note: A is the film rating for adult
mounts are horses for riding

explanation.surface: Taking the size of grown horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts are quantities, and measures as a noun also means quantities.

clue.text: 5 maybe lure man astray

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Five lures a man off the path.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a reference to clue 5; it is simply the number five.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is a number, and its symbol 5 is a figure or digit.

clue.text: Hurry with small beer for rugby player

parts.note: to fly is to rush or hurry
a half is a half-pint, a small measure of beer in a British pub

explanation.surface: A rugby player rushes off for a quick half-pint.
explanation.definitionFit: The fly-half is the rugby union position wearing number 10, the main playmaker behind the scrum.

clue.text: Regular — and what one wears?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means even, consistent, regular
the standard outfit worn by members of a group

explanation.surface: A query about everyday dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform describes something unvarying, and also names prescribed clothing such as a school outfit.

clue.text: At home, taking care of planning

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
tending means looking after or taking care of

explanation.surface: Someone at home caring for others while making plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Intending means having in mind as a plan or purpose.

clue.text: Some town errands for proprietor

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper sends someone out on some errands in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who owns a business or property.

clue.text: Lizard — try grabbing neck but not head

indicators.note: the word for try holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the first letter of neck is dropped

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt to catch a lizard by the neck, but not the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the noun go, as in 'have a go'; 'but not head' beheads neck, and 'grabbing' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small climbing lizard of warm countries.

clue.text: Over 100 casinos prepared for events

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: More than a hundred gambling halls readied for big nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions are special events or happenings.

clue.text: Levi runs off with article in general

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the rearranged letters
off means wrong or spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone named Levi dashes away carrying an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LEVIRUNS to UNIVERSL; 'in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal and general both mean applying to all cases or everyone.

clue.text: Awfully I danced — and it showed

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A confession of terrible dancing that everyone could see.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicated means pointed out or showed.

clue.text: Flipping chose to keep at firm

indicators.note: the turned word holds the next piece inside it
flipping turns the word for chose back to front

parts.note: decided means chose

explanation.surface: Someone flipping a coin decided to stay at the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild British oath; it reverses the word for chose, which 'to keep' then wraps around 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicated and firm both describe steadfast, committed loyalty.

clue.text: Edward upset father's wishes

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the name upside down

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward
a sire is a father, so sire's

explanation.surface: Edward is distressed by what his father wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires as a plural noun means wishes or longings.

clue.text: Entrance dim?

definitions.meaning: to entrance is to enchant or charm
read as ..., to take the light away

explanation.surface: An entry hall that is poorly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight means enchant, and dim playfully means remove light, de-light.

clue.text: Agitate Arab leader by the sound of it

indicators.note: the answer is said like the word for Arab leader

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief or ruler

explanation.surface: A call to stir up an Arab ruler, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake something is to agitate or jolt it.

clue.text: Perhaps a tiny portion with no starter

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for tiny portion is dropped

parts.note: a particle is a tiny portion

explanation.surface: Maybe a small helping without the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a meal; it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word a is the indefinite article in grammar.

clue.text: Serious wear in vest when all tops are removed

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the three words is dropped

explanation.surface: Dressing gravely in a vest, until every shirt comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' looks like clothing; it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in manner.

clue.text: Window attachments badly installed in ship

indicators.note: one piece is fitted inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Window fittings were poorly put in aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sills are the ledges fixed along the bottom of window frames.

clue.text: Bump into Parisian in buffet

parts.note: en is French for in
a buffet is a counter where food is served

explanation.surface: Meeting someone by chance at a Paris buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a verb meaning hit; here it is the serving counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is to meet them by chance, to come across them.

clue.text: Try ales with 50 per cent off, perhaps

indicators.note: losing half of the word ales leaves its back half

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example

explanation.surface: Sample beers at half price, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, so try is its old sense.

clue.text: Those who take drugs giving rise to research in America

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the word for America

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: rise in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: res is a short form of research

explanation.surface: Drug users prompting American research.
explanation.definitionFit: Users is the everyday word for people who take illegal drugs.

clue.text: King, for example, is keeping in contact with realms

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the word is holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: on means touching or resting upon

explanation.surface: A monarch, say, stays in touch with his kingdoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions and realms are both areas or territories.

clue.text: Last bit of breakfast cereal, nuts, syrup

indicators.note: takes the final letter of breakfast
nuts means crazy, so the letters of cereal are scrambled

explanation.surface: A list of the final breakfast items: cereal, nuts, syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like a food here; it rearranges CEREAL into REACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the British name for dark syrup from sugar refining.

clue.text: Please speak about this sofa on a regular basis

indicators.note: the word for speak goes around the other letters

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: every other letter of this sofa is taken

explanation.surface: A polite request to talk about this couch often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of 'this sofa'; 'about' wraps the word for speak round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy or gratify them.

clue.text: Abandon swallowing small sweet

indicators.note: the word for abandon takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Leaving a little sweet uneaten, gulping it down instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is the pudding course, the dessert.
